## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhīrukajātaka* (Ja 132) is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha related this account while staying at Jetavana, occasioned by a sutta treating the temptation by the daughters of Māra beneath the Goat-herds' Banyan tree (*Ajapālanigrodha*); the Buddha opened the discourse by citing the beginning of that sutta, framed around the opening moral line “Wise counsels heeding” [SuttaCentral].

In modern scholarship and printed editions, the text's title varies across manuscript lineages: in V. Fausböll's edition of the *Jātakaṭṭhakathā*, the entry is indexed as *Bhiruka-jātaka* with a cross-reference to *Pañcagaru-jātaka* [Fausböll 1897], and Fausböll notes *Bhirukajātakam* as a reading found in Burmese manuscript witnesses [Fausböll 1877].

SuttaCentral records four translations across four modern languages [SuttaCentral]. Automated analysis by DharmaNexus identified no significant Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language parallels meeting its reporting threshold [DharmaNexus], and no direct parallels in other Buddhist canonical corpora are listed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
